idea.body: Where two chords cross inside a circle, the two products of their pieces are always equal. If chords AC and BD cross at X, then AX times XC equals BX times XD. Where two secants cross outside a circle at an external point P, each secant's near segment times its own whole length gives the same product. PA times PB equals PC times PD. Where a tangent and a secant meet outside a circle, the tangent length squared equals the secant's near segment times its whole length. A wheel's two chords cross with pieces 4 and 9 on one, and 6 and an unknown on the other. Since 4 times 9 is 36, the unknown piece is 36 divided by 6, which is 6.

ways.name: Set up the product equation
ways.when: Use this when two chords cross inside a circle and three of the four pieces are known.
steps: Chords AC and BD cross at point X inside a circle. AX is 5, XC is 12, BX is 6.
Where two chords cross inside a circle, the two products of their pieces are equal.
AX times XC is 5 times 12, which is 60.
Set that equal to BX times XD: 6 times XD equals 60, so XD is 10.
ways.example: Chords AC and BD cross at X. AX = 5, XC = 12, BX = 6. Find XD.
ways.trap: Multiplying a piece from one chord with a piece from the other chord instead of keeping each chord's own two pieces together.

ways.name: Tangent squared equals near times whole
ways.when: Use this when one of the two lines from the outside point is a tangent.
steps: From external point P, a secant has near segment PA = 3 and whole length PB = 27. A tangent touches at T.
Where a tangent and a secant meet outside a circle, the tangent length squared equals near times whole.
The square root of 81 is 9, so PT is 9.
ways.example: From P, a secant has PA = 3 and PB = 27. A tangent from P touches the circle at T. Find PT.
ways.trap: Forgetting to take the square root at the end and leaving 81 as the tangent length.

ways.name: Match the picture to the rule
ways.when: Use this to decide which of the three product rules a problem needs.
steps: Two secants meet at external point P: PA = 4, PB = 16 on one, PC = 8, PD unknown on the other.
Check where the vertex sits: inside the circle uses chords, outside uses secants and tangents.
Two full secants from an outside point: multiply each one's near segment by its own whole length.
4 times 16 is 64, so 8 times PD must also equal 64: PD is 8.
ways.example: Secants from P give PA = 4, PB = 16, and PC = 8 with PD unknown. Find PD.
ways.trap: Multiplying the near segment of one secant by the whole length of the other instead of keeping each secant's own two lengths together.

bank.prompt: A robot's wheel is a circle. Chords AC and BD cross inside it. The crossing point splits AC into pieces of 4 and 9, and splits BD into a piece of 6 on one side. Find the other piece of BD.
explanation: Two chords crossing inside a circle split so the two products of their pieces are equal: 4 times 9 = 6 times the missing piece.
4 times 9 is 36, so the missing piece is 36 divided by 6, which is 6.
hints: The product of one chord's two pieces always equals the product of the other chord's two pieces.
Divide the known product by the given piece to find the missing one.
